text:
Alex K: Quick sync — I'm running experiments for SLO-driven batching where token budget targets vary by route/tier (p95 focus). Sharing early numbers & config, want eyes on kernel selection interactions, KV cache effects, and any perf regressions.

Maria G: Ran a perf sweep on the canary (10% traffic). Short-chat route (route=chat-short, tier=standard) p95 dropped from 210ms -> 155ms. Long-qa route (route=qa-long, tier=standard) p95 bumped 980ms -> 1.12s.

Jordan T: Interesting. Looks like when token_budget_target is low we force the small-kernel path more often; kernel switch + extra memcpy cost adds tail latency for long sequences.

Priya S: Also seeing KV cache hit rate drop on qa-long during the canary. cache_hit_rate: 0.78 -> 0.62 which explains extra decoding work per request. Interleaved batching means multi-turn sessions miss reuse.

Alex K: Config I deployed on canary (snippet):
```
{
  "routes": {
    "chat-short": {"token_budget_target": 32, "batch_timeout_ms": 10, "tier": "standard"},
    "qa-long":   {"token_budget_target": 128, "batch_timeout_ms": 20, "tier": "standard"}
  },
  "queue_policy": "slo_aware_priority"
}
```

Maria G: Profile summary (wall time med/p95):
- chat-short: med 85ms / p95 155ms
- qa-long:   med 420ms / p95 1120ms
CPU/GPU: gpu_util up ~4%, host CPU up ~8% on canary nodes.

Jordan T: Kernel note: when token_budget_target is high we pick the large GEMM kernel optimized for long context; when lowered we pick a smaller kernel which is faster per token but has worse amortization on context switches. We might need to add a "sticky_kernel_hint" so a request keeps kernel choice for its lifetime.

Priya S: FYI KV behavior: continuous batching groups by arrival not session. Proposing a small affinity window (e.g., 50ms) where requests that share session_id get prioritized into the same micro-batch to preserve KV hits. Could reduce p95 for multi-turn routes.

Alex K: Good call. Can we try two orthogonal changes and A/B: (A) slo_aware queue priority (VIP routes first) + token budgets per tier; (B) affinity window to preserve KV locality + sticky_kernel_hint. Run both at 5% each.

Maria G: I'll roll (A) to 5% now and collect p95, tail-kernel-change-rate, cache_hit_rate.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for config 2026-05-14T09:12Z -> 5% traffic.

sre-bot: Alert (threshold): long-qa p95 crossed 1.0s for 2 consecutive 5m windows during initial ramp. Investigating. :eyes:

Jordan T: If alert persists, we should revert token_budget changes for qa-long and only apply affinity window. Kernel-switch metrics are noisy; add per-request kernel-change counter.

Priya S: A couple more observations from traces: batching_size distribution shifted left for qa-long (more small batches) which increased per-batch overhead. affinity window should help. Also KV eviction rate up ~12% on canary caches.

Alex K: Action items:
- Maria: collect these metrics for both A and B at 5% (p95, p50, batch_size_hist, kernel_change_rate, kv_hit, kv_evictions).
- Jordan: prototype sticky_kernel_hint and kernel-change counter (low effort).
- Priya: implement 50ms affinity window flag + telemetry for session-affinity effectiveness.
- I'll hold broader rollout until we see net p95 improvement on long-qa.

Maria G: Ack. I'll post results in this thread in ~30m.

Jordan T: One more thought — try setting token_budget_target as a percentile (token_budget_p95) per-route based on recent token distribution instead of a hard static number. Might adapt better to workload shifts.

Alex K: Love that. Add token_budget_p95 experiment to backlog if A/B inconclusive.

sre-bot: Canary note: after initial ramp metrics stabilized; need 30m steady state for final verdict.

Maria G: Preliminary after 20m: chat-short p95 holds at 150ms, qa-long p95 still ~1.1s. Batch_size median for qa-long moved from 6 -> 3. Kernel_change_rate up 2.5x. Will continue.

Alex K: Thanks all. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
